**Playbook for sonar picket**

**Hiding.** My hidden cell is only guessable if I'm predictable. Rotate cells, prefer edges, and never reuse a cell the enemy has hit or that I've burned repeatedly. Track what my shooter (the boat that fires on me per the standing order) has aimed at and avoid those cells too — they're building an elimination map of me just as I am of my target. Vary fully each round; a rotation pattern is still a pattern.

**Firing.** The standing order fixes my *target*, not my cell. Vary my fire cell each round, uncorrelated with my hide cell. Use the public claim stream as an elimination map: every truthful "miss" on cell n tells me my target wasn't at n; every "hit" on someone tells me exactly where they were. Over rounds this narrows the board — in my episode the target kept missing me and I kept missing the target, which means both of us were randomizing well. Accept that hits are low-probability (I landed 1 of 6) and don't count on them for income. If eliminations accumulate, prefer cells that are unfired AND not adjacent to my own previous guesses, so I cover fresh ground.

**Claims.** The office validates claims against the true result — lying isn't available. Report truthfully, no thought wasted. But read everyone's claims as free location data for my own targeting and evasion.

**Escort — still the biggest prize, but my approach failed.** Mutual escort claims pay 5 points each per round, yet I collected zero across six rounds despite proposing pacts in my notes twice. The problem: the other boats posted only "steady on station" and never engaged. Revisions: (1) Propose in round 1 to *both* other boats, not just one — a specific, verifiable commitment ("Echo will claim Foxtrot if Foxtrot claims Echo") addressed to each, so one unresponsive boat doesn't strand me. (2) Re-propose every round a pact is unconfirmed; a single attempt in round 1 and one in round 6 was far too passive. (3) In the final round, if no pact exists, file an escort claim anyway naming the boat most likely to reciprocate — a unilateral claim costs nothing and pays 5 if they happened to name me. "None" scores zero every time; I submitted "none" repeatedly when an unreciprocated gamble cost me nothing and had upside. Only submit "none" if a wrong claim carries any penalty (it didn't here). (4) Use notes to make my own escort claim predictable: announce "I am claiming Foxtrot as escort this round" so Foxtrot can capture the mutual 5 by naming me back — self-interested signaling beats asking for a pact.

**Harbor.** Harbor offers +3 for firing on it but threatens removal from the board, which destroys all future escort and hit income. Only consider it if I'm far behind in the final round AND no escort payout remains possible. Otherwise never fire on Harbor.

**Notes.** Use them for coordination, not chatter. "Steady on station" from the others told me nothing — expect passive, unresponsive players and plan around them rather than waiting on their cooperation. If notes go unanswered twice, stop asking and start *announcing* my own unilateral actions (escort claims, cell threats) so any reciprocator can lock in the mutual payoff.

**Scoring math.** A hit is +4 to me and only -1 to the target; escort pairs are +5 each and guaranteed if mutual. The escort economy dominates — my entire final score (+4) came from a single lucky hit, and one successful escort round would have matched it. Prioritize escort capture every round, treat shooting as a bonus, and don't over-invest in evasion: being hit costs only 1.

# Playbook — Sonar Picket (Foxtrot seat or similar)

## Hiding
- Avoid repeating the same cell across rounds — opponents pattern-match on repetition. Rotate cells and avoid clustering around any "safe-feeling" number I gravitate toward.
- My upstream neighbor (who fires at me per the standing order) is guessing my cell every round. True randomization beats any heuristic; if I catch myself favoring a cell or a region, break the pattern deliberately.
- NEVER broadcast my hiding cell in a note — I leaked "hiding at cell 3" once and it is pure giveaway with zero payoff. Notes about position should be bluffs or silence.

## Firing
- Don't default to one fire cell. A static shot pattern against a moving target is worthless — vary the fire cell each round.
- Follow the standing order for target selection. Deviating to fire at Harbor is tempting for the 3-point jettison, but Harbor's explicit threat of removal for the rest of the patrol makes it a trap unless I'm already hopeless with nothing to lose.
- If a target has been hit at a cell, they're unlikely to return there; if they've survived somewhere, also deprioritize it. Use hit/miss information relayed in the log to narrow guesses.

## Claiming
- Always claim the true result — the claim must match the private result anyway; nothing is gained by anything else.

## Escort claims
- Mutual escort pays 5 points each — the best income in the game. But a unilateral claim pays NOTHING: both boats must name each other. This is the critical fact I under-weighted.
- Propose the deal once, clearly, in an early note. If the partner reciprocates in their note or their escort claim, lock in and claim them every round. But do not keep proposing to a partner who has ignored me for multiple rounds — I spent all game proposing to Echo, Echo never once escorted me, and I collected zero escort pay while bleeding points from hits.
- Fallback logic: if round 1-2 proposals get no reciprocation, try the other boat as a partner in round 2-3. If nobody reciprocates by mid-game, stop wasting notes on it and either claim the boat most likely to name me (guess their incentive) or claim none — an unreciprocated claim is a wasted move but costs nothing, so a cheap guess at a cooperative partner is still worth making.
- A partner who is hitting me (as Echo did in round 5) is not cooperating — read their shots as evidence about whether the deal is live, and switch partners accordingly.

## Notes
- Use notes for coordination, not filler — but coordination only works if the counterpart responds. Two ignored proposals means the channel is dead for that purpose; switch to deception or silence.
- Never reveal true position information in notes.

## Scoring math to remember
- Hit = +4 to me, −1 to target. Mutual escort = +5 to each of two boats, but ONLY if both claim each other. Being hit = −1 to me. Over 6 rounds, a locked escort deal is the most reliable income; unreciprocated escorting is worth exactly zero.
- My actual result: −1 point, no hits scored, no escort pay collected. The plan was right; the execution failed on the reciprocity check. Fix that first.

## General principle
- Secure the cooperative payout first, then take speculative shots. But cooperative payouts require a willing partner — verify reciprocity early and cheaply, and have an exit when it isn't there. Don't spend the whole game renewing an offer that's been ignored.

# Playbook

**Hiding:** Vary my hide cell each round; never sit on a cell I've used recently. Move after any hit taken. This worked — I took only scattered hits across six rounds. Randomizing beats over-thinking.

**Station notes:** Post a bland, uninformative note ("steady on station"). Never leak my hide cell. Drop the escort-deal proposals in notes — I tried proposing an explicit deal to Echo twice and got no response and no reciprocal escort claim. The other boats are not reading or acting on notes; proposing deals is wasted effort and mildly marks me as the schemer.

**Firing:** Follow the standing order target every round. But random cell choice produced zero hits in six rounds of firing at Echo — pure randomness is leaving too much on the table. Next time: when assigned the same target repeatedly, sweep systematically rather than re-rolling. Fire a fresh cell each round in a planned order (e.g., 5, 4, 6, 3, 7) so I cover the target's plausible cells without repeats. If the office ever tells me I hit target X at cell n, re-fire that cell next time I'm assigned X before resuming the sweep. Never fire the same cell at the same target twice after a confirmed miss — I wasted a shot re-firing cell 5 at Echo in round 5 after a round-1 miss there.

**Do not fire on Harbor.** The 3-point payroll jettison is tempting, but the standing signal threatens removal from the board, forfeiting all future scoring. Never worth it.

**Claims:** Claim exactly what the office tells me — hit or miss, no exceptions. The claim is forced truthful anyway; there's no decision here.

**Escort claims:** Still claim a boat every round — a wrong claim costs nothing, so "none" is strictly dominated. But adjust expectations and targeting: my repeated unilateral claims of Echo produced zero mutual matches all game. Next time, switch my claimed escort when one boat never reciprocates after 2–3 rounds, and try the boat that fires at me (Foxtrot, per the standing order) — an opponent shooting at me has an incentive to buy me off, and a mutual claim cancels the hostility at +5 each. Reassess each round based on who, if anyone, claimed me (the office shows past rounds' escort results if available).

**Endgame:** Don't coast. Final rounds are identical scoring opportunities — keep firing the standing order at a fresh, systematic cell and keep the escort claim live.

**General rule:** Total honesty with the office, point-grabbing everywhere else. This game finished at +0.0: no hits landed and no escort bonus ever landed. The two reliable levers are (1) systematic target-cell coverage instead of random re-rolls, and (2) not sticking with an escort partner who never reciprocates. Fix both.
